public_manager_decisions.body: [A10] Addendum from #969's round 2 (issuecomment-7086009278): with every input bound (the base's path), the registering record at 8x8/1if also produces a work pass **over THE SHARE (2 ms)**, not only over its slice. #977's bound therefore includes THE SHARE: after the fix, no work pass of a registering burst exceeds 2.0 ms at 1x1/1if or 8x8/1if, on the bound path and on #969's kept path. The srp-bound and srp-kept groups (CPU budget harness, PR #971) are the measurement.

[A10] Ruling on the round-1 STOP (owner-delegated decision, 2026-11-23; nothing goes to the owner now).

1. **The registration term counts at the MRP state machines' rate (option a).**
   - IEEE 802.1Q-2018 10.7.11 bounds MRPDUs, not attribute changes.
   - LeaveTime limits only same-kind re-registration: a registrar in LV returns to IN with no new indication.
   - A kind replacement (35.2.6; Milan v1.2 4.2.7.2.2) is immediate, so a legal peer can swap every Talker at each transmit opportunity.
   - No clause gives a lower sustained rate; LeaveAll timing describes a quiet network, not a bound.
   - **Target:** 64 us a Talker, all-in, at 8x8/1if.
2. **The bound:** each record within its slice is not enough; THE SHARE and THE TRANSMIT's build slice must hold under the burst too.
   - THE SHARE is the premise of the 140 ms and 49 ms rows.
   - At the base the mechanism is visible: the first frame at 101 ms, 52 ms past THE TRANSMIT.
3. **Round 2, review-ready by 11-25:**
   - an lwSRP PR beyond opt-exec-1: the buckets, one-port map work, and no validation zeroing, with the refused-allocation difference documented;
   - both adapter cuts;
   - Talker indications marked per sink in the record's pass; ACMP completion and the Listener re-declaration run from the latest kind in their own slices;
   - the transmit merge off at 1x1/1if.
4. **The drain ruling: approved.**
   - A record is charged the unit plus the registration cost times the Talker values it can carry.
   - The count comes from a bound read before parsing, never under it.
   - A record alone in a slice always starts; order is kept and nothing is dropped.
   - The burst group gates the wait within T_svc.
5. **Round 3, by 11-27:** the builds after swaps (sort, re-declares), the copies and zeroing, and a single-delivery replacement, until 64 us is met.
6. **Escalation:** only if on 11-27 the option-(a) load is still over 0.75, or passes exceed THE SHARE, does it go to the owner. The question would be whether 8x8/1if goes to the lab with the swap-rate load over by at most 0.012, as first debt after.

[A10] **Ruling on the round-5 stop.** No owner bound moves.

1. **1x1/1if AECP notice item: restated to 165 us** by the recorded rule: the most measured over every arm and group (15,464 CPU cycles), plus 5 %, rounded up to 5 us. Therefore `AECP_QUEUED_MS` goes from 130 to 135 at 1x1/1if; the queued-notice bound's grid is 5 ms and its ceiling stays the owner's 140 ms.
   - Graded with the item at 165 us: last queued notice 132.95 ms (135); ACMP 29.40 ms (30); txL 47.98 ms (49); ADP 27.79, MAAP 27.89 (30); R5 74.57 and R6 72.69 (90).
   - Recorded: the ACMP margin is 0.60 ms; the next step would reach 140 ms and go to the owner; the code cut stays #908's.
2. **8x8/1if talker-notices: a firmware timing defect, not a grader defect.** A tick posted before the build and counted after it shortens a fresh join timer by up to one centisecond. The grader's model encodes the intended timer and is not changed.
   - The fix is "dispatch pending centiseconds before arming an MRP join timer" (on #1002's branch, `5baf3476`, with its planted control). It comes into #977 with its test.
   - Today's head is the negative control: its ten late run-outs must stay late without the fix.
   - Measured join intervals 187.8 to 190.1 ms stay inside Milan v1.2 Table 4.3.
3. **FR_NFR 3.4.1:** the 0.75 load at 8x8/1if starts the second-hart design study; that study is running, and the owner ruled no second hart for this image. The text keeps 0.75 and records that it was met at 0.757 on 2026-11-25.
4. **tsn-c-stack:** stack main is now `a795471c`. `977-settle` rebases onto it, goes through the stack's own review and merges, and #977 pins that merge commit, never the branch. PR #1016 (stack `a795471c`) lands first.
5. **#977 stays in the coming image.** Without it, a legal registering burst at 8x8/1if has passes over the per-pass share and a first frame past THE TRANSMIT.

[A10] DECISION on round 7's STOP (comment above, posted late on 2026-11-27 after the internal review of PR #993 (finding F4, comment 7210480305); decided 2026-11-26 11:24 CET)

Decider: the manager (A10), under the owner's delegation of lane rulings. The owner bounds are untouched.

Choice: option (a). State `ADP_MBX_LAT_LINK` as 12 (`adp_mbx.h`: 6 + the seed's NOW_MS 1 + 3 + 2; `MAILBOX_SPLIT.md`: `LINK_UP / LINK_DOWN` 12 / 9), with the same define line and table row as PR #1015 (branch `970-discovery`). Take nothing else from #1015: its clock API and its comment describe code this branch doesn't have.

Why (a):
- The extra access is the seed's NOW_MS read, which merged tsn-c-stack PR 40 adds on each exit from DOWN.
- It is one mailbox access on LINK_UP. It is bounded and stated, and the image is byte-identical to the measured one, so no arm has to be re-run.
- Option (b) would hold 11 with an access-free seed. That is a new adapter, a new image, all 498 arm groups and both routes again, to save one stated access.
- #1015 states the same bound, so either PR can land second without a conflict on that line.

Bound: this moves only the stated LINK_UP access count, 11 to 12. It moves no owner bound: last notice 140 ms, ACMP 30 ms, txL 49 ms, loads 0.70 at 1x1/1if and 0.76 at 8x8/1if, THE SHARE 2 ms.

Round 8 implements this (PR #993 at `09599524`).

[A10] RULING on PR #993 after the internal review (comment 7210480305) and the external review (comment 7210572249), owner-delegated. No owner bound moves.

1. **Direction: bound the population.** Splitting a record into pieces is refused. At the ruled rate (2026-11-23, item 1), eighteen registering values per record put the 8x8/1if load near 0.771, over 0.76, however the record is sliced. lwSRP's receive path also re-applies a whole PDU, so it can't resume one part-way.
2. **Rule:** kept Talkers ≤ min(CTRL_SRP_SINKS, V − bound sinks).
   - V is 4 at 1x1/1if, as today, and 9 at 8x8/1if.
   - The charge caps each Talker vector at V, and the bounded-scan fallback at V per 28 octets.
   - The load's registration term counts V per record.
   - Due: 725 µs within the 950 µs slice at 1x1/1if, and 1,500 µs at 8x8/1if.
3. **#969 at 8x8/1if** narrows to one kept Talker per unbound STREAM_INPUT. With every input bound, a rebind to an unregistered Talker completes at the Talker's next declaration, at the latest after a LeaveAll (IEEE 802.1Q-2018 Table 10-3; 10.7.8 NOTE; Milan v1.2 5.5.3.5.18 step 4). Tracked in #1023.
4. **The internal review's F1:** only VectorHeader 0 ends a Message (10.8.1.2). A LeaveAll vector with NumberOfValues 0 skips its header and FirstValue, and the walk continues (10.8.2.8).
5. **Measure** every arm on the built images at both points, with new groups:
   - bound and kept Talkers together at V;
   - a LeaveAll MRPDU in lwSRP's own shape;
   - Lv of the registered kind with New of the other, for every input (35.2.6);
   - more than eight Messages.

   Acceptance: each record stays within its charge, no pass goes over THE SHARE, and slices and builds stay within their statements. Kept stays ≤ bound + 5 %. Costs are restated by the rule, and the load and flip checks pass. Relearn the hot list and route both points.
6. **STOP** and bring it back if any pass exceeds 2 ms, if a restated cost pushes a load or row past its bound, or if #969's tests can't hold at V.

restriction: Prior reports consulted after the independent source verdict and ledger were written; no current-round report by another reviewer consulted.
